description: Search terms and hard filters for routines/search-jobs.md. Copy this file to config/search_keywords.json and edit it. The routine treats it as the ONLY source of search terms and filters. routines/process-tailor-queue.md reads target.output_language from here too. The _comment/_note fields explain why each value is what it is; the agent reads them too.

target.comment: Who and where you are searching for. The demo setup is working-student roles around Cologne, Germany; change all of this to your own situation.
target.output_language_comment: Language of everything the agent writes for you: tailored CVs, cover letters, and the match reasoning in jobs.db. Use the language your applications should be in, e.g. "German" for postings in Germany. If this field is missing, tailoring falls back to the posting's language and search reasoning to English.

broad_sweeps.comment: PRIMARY source of recall, run through the Apify actor. Keep these bare (employment type only). Keyword search on most job boards matches title AND description, so a bare term surfaces roles whose titles you could never predict. Do NOT add tech qualifiers here: narrowing happens at the scoring stage, not the search stage.

priority_searches.comment: Indeed MCP only. Indeed returns about 10 results per query with no pagination, so a bare query returns 10 arbitrary rows and wastes the call. Indeed therefore needs many narrow queries: the opposite of the broad-sweep strategy above.

hard_filters.must_contain_comment: Check against title AND description combined. Some sources return a truncated title, and the real title only appears in the body, so a title-only check is unreliable.
hard_filters.title_exclude_comment: Matched as substrings, so every entry must be specific enough to be unambiguous. A bare 'sales' would also match 'After Sales' and throw away a strong data/AI role before it was ever scored.

title_exclude_override.comment: Exclusion is a demotion signal, not a kill switch. If the title OR the description contains any token below, skip title_exclude entirely and send the job to scoring: the match_score gate reads the whole description and is a far better judge than a substring match on a title.

hard_filters.max_days_posted_comment: Casting wide on keywords multiplies the candidate pool, so the recency window keeps each run reviewable. Postings found late are often already closed.
hard_filters.location_comment: A job passes if its location is in location_include or within location_radius_km of home_location, and not in location_exclude.

apify._actor_note: Any Apify actor that returns job listings (title, company, location, url, posted date, description) works. Check the actor's own input schema and put its fields into actor_input.

actor_input._note: Actor-specific. Map the target above (location, radius, recency) onto whatever fields your actor accepts. The routine adds the sweep term as the keyword field.

apify._cost_note: Many job actors bill per result, often with a minimum per run. Set max_total_charge_usd as a hard cap on every call and don't raise the item count without a reason.

indeed._note: search_jobs(search, location, country_code). Indeed short links can rotate per request, so the same posting may come back with a new URL: dedupe on company+title too (see the routine).

min_match_score_comment: Jobs scoring below this are never inserted, only logged. core/export_dashboard_data.py applies the same threshold (MIN_MATCH_SCORE) as a second safety net; keep the two in sync.
